brief.recommendation: Checkout success 27% vs 95% SLO; $13,493/min at risk. Blocker idle in transaction 115.9s (DB-4), exceeding 60s tolerance. audit.report: The batch_replayable_price_sync job (pid 156822) entered an idle transaction running SELECT 1, blocking 12 sessions and causing checkout success to drop to 27% against a 95% SLO. Revenue was at ~$13,493/min with at most 60s of degraded checkout tolerated. After three rounds, the guardians agreed to terminate the blocker, ending $132k+ in accumulated loss and resolving the lock wait. The database is now cleared, though checkout SLO remains unmet in the verification window.
audit.root_cause: A batch_worker transaction for batch_replayable_price_sync became idle in transaction after 11.6s, holding locks that blocked 12 sessions and degrading checkout well beyond the 60s business tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: The continuity guardian repeatedly rejected the wait proposal because it exceeded the 60s degradation tolerance, correctly surfacing the cost impact. The database guardian eventually shifted to termination in R3, aligning with the continuity guardian's preference once change-calendar clearance was confirmed.
follow_ups: Run a post‑termination checkout test to confirm whether the SLO can be met without the price_sync job.
Add a dashboard alert when a batch_replayable_price_sync session is idle in transaction for >30s to trigger an early termination review.
Document the change-calendar clearance check as a mandatory precondition for R1 waits on may_interrupt batch jobs.
